text:
maria-ng: fwd from customer via support form — after a region failover their requests started getting garbled tokens and quality drop. says latency spiked to 800ms then a second request routed to another region returned a different model variant and produced 'UnknownToken' errors. attaching logs they pasted.

maria-ng: customer report snippet:
```
Request ID: req_9a7b3
Region: eu-west-1 -> auto-reroute -> us-west-2
Model requested: redwood-xl-v2
Served model: redwood-lite-v1
Error: TokenizerError: unknown token id 50260
Latency: 820ms (first), 110ms (second)
```

maria-ng: they say they did not set region explicitly — rely on default routing. started happening after a deploy last night.

ops-bot: auto-route event log: route_policy=latency_based, fallback_enabled=true, fallback_candidates=[redwood-xl-v2, redwood-medium-v1, redwood-lite-v1]

tom-chen: quick check — the lite variant uses an older tokenizer/vocab (vocab_size=50257) vs xl-v2 (vocab_size=50263) so that explains unknown token ids. why did routing pick lite? looks like capacity shortage in eu-west-1 triggered cross-region fallback and then smallest compatible candidate returned because of fastest cold start.

kevin-r: confirm. model registry shows redwood-lite-v1 is labeled 'compat:embedding,gen' but tokenizer metadata mismatched. our compatibility check currently only compares model architecture, not tokenizer vocab size.

maria-ng: customer is escalating. they say outputs are corrupted (HTML escapes, token junk) and billing shows two successful calls. they want immediate mitigation and a repro so they can test.

tom-chen: mitigation options: 1) force-route by region header for their account (quick config) 2) disable cross-region fallback for VIP accounts 3) pin model version to redwood-xl-v2. recommend pin+disable fallback as immediate.

kevin-r: also add a short-term policy update: when fallback candidate tokenizer_vocab_size != requested.tokenizer_vocab_size, mark as incompatible and skip. will push a hotfix to routing service to check model.metadata.tokenizer.vocab_size before promoting fallback.

maria-ng: customer asked for repro steps. tom/kevin can we supply a minimal repro they can run? include curl.

tom-chen: repro (useful to run from eu-west IP):
```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-v2","prompt":"hello world","max_tokens":10}'
# When eu-west-1 capacity low, service may reroute to us-west-2 and pick a smaller variant.
```

kevin-r: temp workaround for customer: set header `X-Route-Policy: no-fallback` or use `model:"redwood-xl-v2@20260210"` to pin exact version. Also advise adding `accept_tokenizer_mismatch:false` (we don't yet support that param in public API but support team can set account flag).

maria-ng: customer accepted pin+no-fallback. they asked for ETA on fix to avoid recurrence.

kevin-r: ETA: push hotfix to routing checks today (low-risk) — will also add a monitoring alert for tokenizer mismatch rate > 0.1% per minute. full rollout to include model compatibility matrix sync next week.

tom-chen: I'll update the routing config: disable selecting candidates with tokenizer_vocab_size mismatch in the fast path. deploying canary now.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: routing-service/canary -> started (canary_id=canary-20260307-12).

maria-ng: thanks. I'll reply to customer with repro steps, immediate pin instructions, and note that we've started a canary fix. will request they confirm after we disable fallback.

kevin-r: follow-up note for engineering: we should also audit tokenizer version tags in model registry and ensure model variants include `tokenizer_hash` in metadata for robust equality checks (not just vocab_size).

maria-ng: adding to thread: customer will test in next hour and we will monitor. will post results here. :working_on_it: 

maria-ng: update (after 45m) — customer confirmed that pinning to redwood-xl-v2@20260210 fixed the errors and quality returned to normal. latency still slightly elevated since requests stayed in eu-west-1 but no token errors.

kevin-r: closing loop: can we add a short postmortem note in incidents if canary shows full success? I'll draft a short doc with root cause (incompatible tokenizer selected as fallback due to coarse compatibility check) and remediation (routing guard + registry metadata enrichment).

maria-ng: agreed. leaving this thread open until canary passes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
